title: MPI Communication Performance on AMD MI300A: Microbenchmarks and Applications
problem: AMD MI300A integrates CPU and GPU chiplets with shared HBM3; traditional host-device boundary assumptions invalidated; little guidance on MPI library behavior on this novel architecture
motivation: Early MI300A deployments lack performance characterization; need practical guidance for MPI optimization on APU architectures
method: The AMD MI300A combines CPU and GPU on one chip with shared memory, which differs from traditional systems where CPU and GPU are separate. The researchers tested how four MPI libraries—MVAPICH-Plus, Open MPI, MPICH, and Cray MPICH—perform on MI300A nodes by running microbenchmarks that measure simple message-passing, multi-node coordinated operations, and scaling behavior. They validated their findings with real applications: OpenFOAM for computational fluid dynamics and LLM distributed training.
key_novelty: This is the first comprehensive measurement of how MPI communication performs on AMD MI300A chips, which integrate CPU and GPU with shared memory.
contributions: Point-to-point performance analysis on CPU and GPU buffers
Application-level performance validation with HPC and ML workloads
limitations: Abstract does not provide specific performance numbers or detailed bottleneck analysis
